title: Cross-tenant Data Scrubbing and Ephemeral Credentials Playbook
author: Anika Patel
content:
Summary
=======
This playbook defines the required configuration, operator procedures, and validation tests for implementing cross-tenant data scrubbing and ephemeral credentials in Redwood private deployments (VPC and on‑prem). It codifies a minimal operator-safe path for preventing accidental tenant data leakage in shared runtime paths, and for ensuring credentials used by operators and field agents are short‑lived and auditable.

Goals
-----
- Prevent cross-tenant exposure in control and data plane (KV cache, logging, telemetry ingest).
- Provide an operator workflow for provisioning, rotating, and revoking ephemeral credentials.
- Define scrubbing rules and verification steps to remove tenant identifiers from sampled logs and telemetry before they leave customer-controlled networks.
- Provide rollback and incident procedures for failures during rollout.

Scope and exclusions
--------------------
- Applies to Redwood Private (VPC & on‑prem) deployments where multiple tenant namespaces share runtime services (e.g., shard-level KV caches, telemetry gateways).
- Excludes single-tenant physically isolated appliances where no shared runtime exists.

Terminology
-----------
- tenant-id: canonical customer tenant identifier (opaque string).
- ephemeral-cred: short-lived operator/service credential issued by redwood-ephemeral-agent.
- scrub-agent: sidecar process that sanitizes logs/telemetry prior to egress.
- control-plane-proxy: platform component that brokers control operations (pin, swap, rollout).

Prerequisites
-------------
| Component | Minimum version | Owner | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| redwood-operator-cred-proxy | v1.8.0 | eng-private-deployments | issues ephemeral tokens scoped by tenant and role |
| scrub-agent (sidecar) | v0.9.2 | eng-private-deployments | supports regex + structured field rewrite policies |
| telemetry-ingest | v2.4.1 | eng-platform | supports pre-ingest filters and allowlists |
| audit-log-collector | v3.1.0 | eng-sre | configurable retention and signed entries |

Security requirements (high level)
---------------------------------
1. All operator credentials MUST be ephemeral (max TTL 1h by default).
2. Any log/trace/metric payload exported outside the tenant vpc must pass through scrub-agent and a whitelist filter.
3. KV cache keys and model metadata must be namespaced by tenant and never forwarded to a shared telemetry bucket without tokenization.

Design summary
--------------
- Ephemeral credential flow: operator authenticates to customer SSO -> requests ephemeral token via redwood-operator-cred-proxy (scoped TTL) -> token minted and logged to audit-log-collector -> operator uses token to perform runtime actions through control-plane-proxy.
- Scrubbing flow: runtime components emit structured telemetry -> local scrub-agent applies per-tenant rules (field removal, tokenization) -> telemetry-ingest receives sanitized payload and applies global allowlists -> samples forwarded to Redwood observability/console.

Operator checklist (pre-deployment)
----------------------------------
- [ ] Confirm redwood-operator-cred-proxy v1.8.0 is installed and reachable over mTLS.
- [ ] Deploy scrub-agent sidecar to all runtime pods that emit tenant-identifying fields.
- [ ] Update telemetry-ingest config with tenant allowlist and global redact rules.
- [ ] Configure audit-log-collector to store signed entries in customer-controlled storage with retention 90 days (default).

Step-by-step procedures
-----------------------
A. Configure and validate ephemeral credential service
1. Install redwood-operator-cred-proxy: helm upgrade --install redwood-operator-cred-proxy redwood/chart/operator-cred --version 1.8.0 --set tls.enabled=true
2. Create operator role bindings for the customer operator groups (example):
   ```yaml
   apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
   kind: RoleBinding
   metadata:
     name: customer-ops-scoped
     namespace: redwood-system
   subjects:
     - kind: Group
       name: customer-ops@example.com
   roleRef:
     kind: Role
     name: operator-scoped-role
     apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
   ```
3. Configure TTL policy in the proxy: set max_ttl_seconds=3600 and default_refresh=false.
4. Test mint flow (operator machine):
   - curl -X POST https://redwood-operator-cred-proxy.internal/v1/mint -H "Authorization: Bearer <SSO-JWT>" -d '{"tenant":"tenant-123","role":"operator"}'
   - Expect response {"token":"ephem_...","expires_in":3600} and an audit-log entry with fields [requester, tenant, role, trace_id].
5. Verify token revocation: revoke token via API and observe control-plane-proxy rejecting requests with revoked token within 30s.

B. Deploy and validate scrub-agent
1. Sidecar deployment: add the scrub-agent container to the pod template with configSecret reference (example snippet in /etc/scrub/config.yaml).
2. Example scrub rules (config.yaml):
   ```yaml
   rules:
     - name: remove-tenant-id
       match: "$.request.tenant_id"
       action: remove
     - name: mask-email
       match: "$.user.email"
       action: mask
       mask_char: "*"
       keep_last: 3
   ```
3. Apply test: emit a sample log with tenant_id and confirm scrub-agent transforms it prior to TCP TLS egress.
4. Unit tests: run scrub-agent --validate-config against policy set; expected: exit 0 and a warning-free output.

C. Canary rollout and traffic migration
1. Canary slice: pick 2% of tenant traffic (canary-tenants list) and enable scrub-agent + ephemeral-cred enforcement only for that slice.
2. Monitor metrics for 48 hours: 
   - telemetry-ingest.error_rate < 0.05%
   - control-plane-proxy.auth_failures < 0.1 per minute per cluster
   - operator action latency increase < 150ms (p50)
3. If any metric exceeds threshold, execute rollback procedure (see section "Rollback and remediation").
4. After 48 hours and validation, expand in geometric steps: 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%, validating at each stage.

Validation tests and verification
--------------------------------
- Functional checks:
  1. Emit post-scrubbing sample and assert tenant_id not present in payload via curl to local-scrub-proxy.
  2. Verify ephemeral token rejection after MMC (Manual Revocation) within 30s.
- End-to-end tests:
  - Run synthetic workload (1000 requests/sec) against control-plane-proxy and confirm no increase in 5xxs > 0.2%.
- Audit checks:
  - Spot-check 10 signed audit entries weekly for token issuance and revocation pairs.

Operational metrics and SLOs
--------------------------
- Token issuance latency: p99 < 200ms (SLO).
- Scrub-agent processing latency added: p95 < 30ms per request.
- False-negative scrubs (post-deploy) target: 0; acceptable < 0.01% before escalation.
- Audit log completeness: every ephemeral token action must have an audit entry; missing entries > 0 triggers immediate investigation.

Rollback and remediation
------------------------
Triggers for rollback:
- Canary metrics breach (see Canary rollout thresholds).
- Reproducible data leakage verified by audit or customer report.
- Major functional regression (control-plane auth failures > 1/min sustained for 5m).
Rollback steps:
1. Revoke newly issued ephemeral tokens via redwood-operator-cred-proxy revoke endpoint.
2. Disable scrub-agent at pod-level by toggling annotation: redwood.scrub.enable=false and trigger rolling restart.
3. Revert redwood-operator-cred-proxy configuration to previous release using helm rollback <release> <revision>.
4. Engage incident triage: open Incident ticket with priority P1, assign oncall and security owner.

Forensic evidence preservation
-----------------------------
- Preserve audit-log-collector bundle (signed) and store a copy in customer-provided S3/GCS with read-only ACL.
- Take snapshot of scrub-agent configuration and telemetry-ingest allowlists.
- Export control-plane-proxy auth traces (redaction applied) for analysis.

Roles and ownership
-------------------
- Security (owner): policy, verification, and post-incident review.
- Eng-private-deployments (operator lead): deployment, canary execution, day‑2 maintenance.
- Eng-sre: metrics collection, alerting, and runbook automation.
- Customer ops: approval for rollout and access to audit bundles.

Templates and operator commands
------------------------------
- Mint ephemeral token (example CLI):
  redwoodctl auth mint --tenant tenant-123 --role operator --ttl 3600
- Revoke token by id:
  redwoodctl auth revoke --token-id ephem_abcd1234
- Validate scrub-agent config:
  kubectl exec -n redwood-system $(kubectl get pod -l app=scrub-agent -o name | head -n1) -- /usr/local/bin/scrub-agent --validate /etc/scrub/config.yaml

Appendix: Example scrub-agent regexp checklist
--------------------------------------------
- Remove exact tenant_id patterns: /tenant-[0-9a-f]{8}/i
- Mask UUIDs in metadata keys longer than 24 chars: replace with first 8 chars + "..."
- Tokenize email addresses to username-hash@example.invalid

Contact and escalation
----------------------
- Primary oncall (security): pager: sec-oncall@redwood.internal, Slack: #sec-oncall
- Operator lead: eng-private-deployments@redwood.internal
- For legal/data questions: legal-privacy@redwood.internal

End of playbook.
